title: Align credential TTL and async-iterable ergonomics across Python/TS/Go SDKs
author: Priya Nair
description: Context: customer integrations and internal examples exposed small mismatches between SDK credential cache TTLs and streaming consumer ergonomics (Python async iterators, TS async generators, Go pull/push stream helpers). Those mismatches caused edge-case double-refreshes under bursty traffic and made cross-language examples diverge. This PR synchronizes the credential TTL/resync heuristics, tightens default retry windows for auth failures, and polishes ergonomic surfaces for async iterables across the three SDKs. Motivation: reduce spurious token refreshes, avoid duplicate background refreshes when a consumer drains and reconnects, and provide idiomatic, consistent examples for docs and Quickstarts. Changes: 1) Introduce unified credential TTL configuration: default TTL window set to 55s of token lifetime for prefetch heuristics with a per-SDK override knob (env/config). 2) Align reauth backoff preset for transient 401/403 to a shared 'sdk-auth' retry bundle (5s, 15s, 45s) with jitter. 3) Python: add AsyncStream.peek() helper and explicit close semantics to avoid implicit refresh race on garbage collection; update session manager to coalesce concurrent refreshes. 4) TypeScript: expose generator.buffered() for line-buffered consumers and ensure reauth is idempotent across repeated pull calls; add small ergonomic rename for clarity (pull -> nextChunk kept as alias for backward compat). 5) Go: implement cred debounce layer in credcache.go to collapse rapid refresh requests and add lightweight ConnPool. 6) Tests: cross-lang e2e harness updated to simulate burst reconnects and assert single refresh per token window. 7) Docs/Examples: update three quickstarts to use new helpers and call out the config knobs. Compatibility notes: backward-compatible surface maintained; TS alias preserves old API names, Python changes are additive (peek/close) and do not remove existing methods, Go adds a new small package for pool management. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for token coalescing and retry backoff - [x] Integration e2e harness against local devserver simulating short-lived tokens - [x] Docs updated and example snippets tested - [x] Benchmarked under 10k req/s simulated bursts (no additional spurious refreshes observed) - [x] Security review for credential caching (no secrets persisted to disk) Testing instructions: run sdk-e2e/harness/run_local.sh then run three SDK clients in the harness directory; see README in e2e for assertions. Impact: reduces token refresh churn under bursty traffic and reduces 401 cascades during short token lifetimes. Related: ENG-3479 (streaming stability), ENG-3301 (auth backoff consistency).

review_comments: Alex Rivera (reviewer): Nice consolidation. Question: why 55s for TTL window? Can we derive from token lifetime instead of hardcoding a number?

Priya Nair (author): We compute window as max(ceil(lifetime*0.1),55) for short-lived tokens; 55s was chosen from empirical tests with 60s lifetimes to avoid immediate refresh storms. Added comment in code and docs to explain formula.
Jinsoo Park (reviewer): In Go, ConnPool looks good but watch the mutex on borrow/return for hot paths. Could you add a microbenchmark?
Priya Nair (author): Added go microbench in conn/pool_bench_test.go and tuned the borrow path to use sync.Pool for light-weight cases; results appended in the PR CI artifact.
Maria Gomez (reviewer): TS rename 'pull -> nextChunk' concerns me for semver. Is aliasing sufficient to avoid breakage for frameworks?
Priya Nair (author): We keep pull as an exported alias to nextChunk and added deprecation comment with a one-minor bump note in changelog; tests cover both names.
CI Bot: e2e harness failed first run due to race in Python session coalescer under heavy concurrent refresh attempts; reworked lock-free path and retriggered; tests now pass.
Security Team: quick scan looks good, no secrets written to logs or disk; well documented TTL knobs.
release_notes: SDKs: aligned credential prefetch TTL heuristics and added ergonomic async iterable helpers. Python: AsyncStream.peek and explicit close to avoid refresh races. TypeScript: buffered() helper and nextChunk alias; auth retry presets unified. Go: credential debounce and ConnPool added. No breaking changes; minor API aliasing note for TS.
notes_for_release_manager: Merge via squash. Notify SDK maintainers to schedule language-specific patch releases (Python 2.5.1, TS 1.29.0, Go 1.8.0). Update changelogs in each SDK before publish.
testing_summary: Unit+integration+bench: unit coverage increased for auth modules, e2e burst tests confirm single refresh per token window in >95% of runs, minor flakiness fixed and re-run.
